note: Resident memory and cost of ONE factorised two-die 3D-ICE session, measured on node-06-8xv100 (96 CPU, 243 GB) under slurm job 1320, OMP_NUM_THREADS=1, 25 Aug 2026. The catalogue re-run parallelises by system matrix and each concurrent stream holds its own factorisation, so this is what bounds concurrency. It was previously a guess.
finding: At 34-core the node holds ~85 sessions, so concurrency is bound by the 96 CPUs, not by memory -- the re-run can use the whole node. At 128-core it is 16 sessions and memory binds first. Peak RSS runs ~1.3x steady-state RSS, which is the factorisation's transient; sizing on steady RSS would over-subscribe the node.
projection: The 128-core solve-only time of 1.916 s confirms the ~2 s projected in solve_cost_two_die.json from the smaller dies' near-linear trend.
